title: Console backlog surgical prioritization — sprint 19
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for a surgical backlog pruning session ahead of Sprint 19. We aim to reduce the active console/tooling backlog by ~30% of items currently targeting M+ (medium-to-long) timelines, by either: (a) grooming to actionable work for next two sprints, (b) deferring with clear criteria, or (c) closing as out-of-scope. This doc captures heuristics, triage rules, quick-wireframe notes, and the final sprint cut plan.

Context and constraints:
- Sprint window: Sprint 19 (2026-06-22 to 2026-07-05) — two-week cadence.
- Team capacity estimate: 6 FTE frontend, 3 FTE backend, 1 UX, 0.5 PM. Reserve 20% capacity for ops/bug cycle.
- Drivers for pruning: latency SLO regressions from new model routing (CONSOLE-3421), increase in support tickets for route creation UX, and customer asks for per-route cost breakdown visibility.
- Acceptance principle: Anything that remains in the backlog after pruning must have a) owner, b) target milestone or a deferral tag, c) measurable success metric or clear reason for long-term hold.

Triage heuristics (surgical):
1) User impact first: prioritize items tied to active customer pain, high-severity bugs, or features that unblock sales/Dedicated deals. Use Jira labels customer-facing / blocker.
2) Cost vs. benefit: estimate rough engineering hours (T-shirt 1/2/4/8 days). Items > 8d without explicit ROI must be decomposed or deferred.
3) Risk to SLOs: any item that mitigates latency/error regressions gets elevated priority.
4) Cross-team dependency: if item needs infra/serving-runtime changes and no explicit alignment ticket exists, downgrade until dependency is resolved.
5) Quick wins: add a bucket for sub-2d low-risk UX fixes to clear user friction and reduce support volume.

Priority buckets defined:
- P0 (Sprint must): high-severity bug or customer-blocking feature; estimate <= 8d total; has owner and acceptance.
- P1 (Target sprint): important feature/enhancement that meaningfully improves observability or onboarding; estimate <= 8d or decomposed into sub-tasks.
- P2 (Backlog groom): nice-to-have; scheduled for grooming next quarter; requires PO approval to push to P1.
- P3 (Park/Close): low ROI, deprecated, or duplicate. Closing requires comment and alternate tracking (epic or parking-lot label).

Grooming session plan (60–90m):
- Prework (owner): pre-tag tickets with quick estimate and initial label (customer-facing / infra-dep / UX-wireframe).
- 15m: Quick sync on goals and capacity.
- 30–45m: Rapid triage by ticket: owner reads short description, team calls vote (A = do in sprint / B = decompose + schedule / C = defer/close). Capture reason.
- 15m: Finalize sprint scope, assign owners, create sub-tasks for decomposed items, and mark deferred items with deferral reason and review date.

Wireframe / UX quick notes (text sketches for tickets):
- Route creation flow (CONSOLE-3489): add inline cost estimate card on step 2 (model + quantization selection). Card shows 3-line breakdown: estimated tokens/hr, cost/hr, preferred batch size suggestion. Acceptance: mock + 1 usability check, no backend required for MVP (use static cost model).
- Per-route analytics drill-in: landing table should allow inline expand for 7d latency histogram + top 3 error classes. Wireframe: table row chevron -> small panel with sparkline and list. Metric latency bucket definition to align with SRE SLA page.
- Rollout canary toggles: add single control to UI that opens the rollout modal; default option 'auto-fallback' toggled on. Default text copy to align with legal.

Example triage decisions (representative):
- CONSOLE-3471 "Route creation confusing dropdowns" — estimate 2d, label UX, decision: P0 quick win. Owner: Marcus Lee. Subtask: adjust labels, AB test copy.
- CONSOLE-3456 "Add KV cache monitoring" — estimate 6d + infra coordination, decision: P1 but blocked by INFRA-1220. Action: create dependency ticket and assign to infra lead.
- CONSOLE-3380 "Unified billing export CSV" — estimate 8d, product ask but low immediate customer pain, decision: P2 groom. Owner: Priya Shah.
- CONSOLE-3322 "Deprecated chat widget cleanup" — low ROI, duplicate, decision: P3 close. Add comment referencing CONSOLE-3000.

Sprint 19 proposed cut (finalized scope):
Committed (P0/P1 top):
- CONSOLE-3471: Route dropdown UX (P0) — 2d
- CONSOLE-3489: Inline cost card (MVP) (P1) — 3d front + 1d copy
- CONSOLE-3456: KV cache monitoring (unblock + design) (P1, partial) — 3d front + create INFRA dep
- CONSOLE-3498: Support triage dashboard quick filters (P1) — 2d

Backlog to groom next cycle (P2):
- Unified billing export CSV (CONSOLE-3380)
- Per-route deep analytics (spike required)
- Rollout experiment templating

Park/close (P3) — examples:
- Small visual polish tickets with no owner or duplicate endpoints (bulk-close set).

Definition of done checklist (for sprint boarding):
- Ticket has owner and at least one acceptance criteria expressed as metric or UI state.
- Estimation field populated and any infra deps listed.
- UX wireframes attached for items with visible changes.
- QA smoke steps and a rollback/fallback plan for features touching rollout or routing.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: infra dependency could stall KV monitoring (CONSOLE-3456). Mitigation: split spike to unblock front-end work and create clear INFRA SLA for review (72h).
- Risk: scope creep on cost-card to connect live pricing. Mitigation: MVP static model and separate ticket for live pricing integration.

Next actions (owners):
- Ava Chen: finalize sprint board and create sub-tasks for decomposed P1 items (due 2026-06-16).
- Marcus Lee: implement CONSOLE-3471 changes and prepare AB test (start 2026-06-22).
- Priya Shah: schedule customer validation call for cost-card copy (by 2026-06-18).
- Rafael Morales: create INFRA-1220 dependency ticket and tag infra lead for 24h review.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — lean on the heuristics in the triage section when voting. If you disagree with a P3 close, annotate the ticket with the reason and propose an owner.
- We should run a retro after Sprint 19 focused on the effectiveness of the surgical pruning session: did we hit the ~30% active backlog reduction target, and did throughput improve?

Appendix (quick glossary):
- M+: medium+ timeline (anything scheduled beyond next two sprints).
- KV cache monitoring: observability for prefix/KV hits used by model caching layer.
- Auto-fallback: runtime policy to fall back to smaller model variant on latency SLO breach.

End of document.
